task_1.title: Stabilize platform requirement revisions without forcing new binaries
task_1.description: Conan 2.26.1 changes platform requirement resolution so platform-provided dependencies and tool dependencies have a stable revision identity in graph and lock data, while the default platform revision no longer changes downstream package IDs. This avoids unnecessary missing-binary situations after upgrading unless the user explicitly pins a platform revision.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 2.26.1 does not create avoidable missing binaries for consumers that use platform requirements or platform tool requirements without an explicit revision, while preserving correct revision-aware behavior when a revision is explicitly declared.

expectation.grounded: Dependencies resolved through `[platform_requires]` and `[platform_tool_requires]` must retain a concrete resolved reference revision for graph, range-resolution, and lockfile identity. If the platform entry does not specify a revision, the resolved reference should use the default platform revision marker. That default marker must be ignored when recipe revisions participate in downstream package ID computation, but an explicit user-provided revision on the platform dependency must remain visible and continue to affect package ID and lock matching where recipe revisions are part of the selected package ID mode.
expectation.conceptual: Platform-supplied dependencies should resolve consistently as a specific dependency reference, including revision identity, but the system must not treat the implicit platform revision as a real recipe change that forces consumers to rebuild. If the user explicitly pins a revision, that explicit revision should still behave like a normal pinned revision.

constraints.grounded: Do not change behavior for explicitly pinned platform revisions: explicit revisions must still be preserved in resolved references and must still participate in downstream package ID calculation in modes that include recipe revisions. Do not let the default platform revision introduce new package IDs or missing binaries for existing consumers that previously depended on revisionless platform references. Range-based platform resolution must keep the selected version and its resolved revision aligned.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve compatibility for existing platform-based consumers and avoid unnecessary rebuild churn. Only explicit user intent to pin a revision should change revision-sensitive identity; the implicit platform default should remain transparent for binary compatibility.

behavior: A platform requirement or platform tool requirement resolved without an explicit revision now carries a stable default platform revision in its resolved reference identity.
When a platform requirement is resolved from a version range, the resolved reference now includes the selected revision identity instead of only the selected version.
The implicit default platform revision is excluded from downstream package ID inputs, so consumers do not get new package IDs solely because the platform dependency now has a default revision marker.
If the platform dependency explicitly includes a revision, that revision remains part of the resolved reference and continues to influence downstream package IDs in revision-sensitive modes.
Lockfile and dependency matching behavior use the resolved platform revision identity consistently, including the default platform revision marker when no explicit revision was supplied.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer uses a platform requirement or platform tool requirement without an explicit revision, the resolved dependency should have a stable platform revision identity rather than remaining revisionless.
When a platform requirement is satisfied through a version range, the final resolved dependency reference should preserve both the chosen version and the chosen revision identity.

When upgrading from 2.26.0 to 2.26.1, consumers that rely on platform requirements without explicit revisions should continue reusing existing binaries instead of appearing as missing solely because of the implicit platform revision.

When a user explicitly pins a platform dependency revision, the resolved dependency should preserve that exact revision and downstream revision-sensitive package ID behavior should continue to reflect it.
When a lockfile or graph records platform-provided dependencies, entries without an explicit user-pinned revision should consistently use the default platform revision identity.
